title: Component manifest
description: One component's contract. Everything the library ships for that component — its CSS, its documentation page, its type declarations, and (later) its Vue wrapper — is generated from this file. It is deliberately framework-neutral: a CSS generator reads the class names, a component generator reads the variant and prop names.

id.description: Directory name under components/, and the slug in the docs URL.

name.description: English name, as Element Plus would print it.

category.description: The group it is listed under in the docs. The categories are Element Plus's, so the two libraries can be compared side by side.

element.description: The native element this component is built on. A component that names an element can be written without JavaScript.

since.description: The version the component appeared in.

style.description: The component's stylesheet, relative to its own directory. The build concatenates these in catalogue order.

base.description: The class every instance carries, e.g. um-button.

also.description: Other base classes the same component paints, for a component that covers a family of native controls — um-textarea and um-select beside um-input. A class listed here is one an instance may carry instead of the base class, never in addition to it.

modifier.description: Prefix for variant and size modifiers, e.g. um-button--.

part.description: Prefix for element parts, e.g. um-button__.

variants.description: The visual variants. Each becomes a modifier class.

state.description: How the variant is painted. Solid carries a fill, soft carries a tint, outline carries a border, ghost carries neither.

states.description: The states a component can be in. A native state names the CSS pseudo-class; a custom state names a class.

selector.description: The selector that carries this state in the stylesheet, e.g. ':disabled' or '.is-loading'. The build checks that it is actually there.

native.description: True when the state comes from a real form element, so it needs no JavaScript.

parts.description: The inner elements of the component. Each becomes a part class.

props.description: The public API. In the CSS-only library a prop is a class; a component wrapper turns the same list into real props.

examples.description: The live examples on the documentation page. The markup is stored here so the page never has to be written by hand.

markup.description: The HTML shown on the page.
